decisions.reason: §1 attributes the failure to fs-ext@2.1.1's install script (node-gyp configure build) pulled by dsh-session-persistence-jsonl, dying at missing Visual Studio/MSVC — a specific dependency/build-phase attribution, not pnpm or network flakiness.

§2 explains the top-level static flock import forces fs-ext's entry (and its native binding) to load on Windows before any branch selection, so --ignore-scripts only moves the failure from install to boot and cannot yield a working service.

§3 distinguishes the win32 named kernel semaphore (acquireLockHandleWin32, no flock, no lock file) from POSIX flock(2); the never-executed Windows fs-ext path permits an import-safe stub while Windows locking stays on the semaphore and POSIX keeps real flock — branch meaning explicit.

§4 follows the node-pty patchedDependencies precedent: win32-gated install script skipping node-gyp, entry rewritten to import-safe callable stubs on win32 with the native module untouched on POSIX, registered in pnpm-workspace.yaml, plus reinstall, module-load, service-boot, and semaphore-lock verification steps.
The plan explicitly honors the owner's no-VS constraint and uses the repo-managed pnpm patch while explicitly rejecting forking/republishing upstream or hand-editing node_modules.

The report connects the DSH-0.1.3-A1- prefix to the fs-ext failure and patch plan but never cites the full card DSH-0.1.3-A1-03 — it self-reports the index was unavailable and invents a slug from the task name.

caps.reason: Installing VS is listed only as a rejected alternative; the affirmative plan needs no MSVC.
--ignore-scripts is explicitly rejected in §2; the plan makes the statically imported entry loadable.
Uses the repository-managed pnpm patch; upstream fork/republish is rejected.
Windows stubs throw if ever called and the named semaphore is kept; POSIX retains real flock — no weakening of write ownership.
